sources.news_title: Jack Smith Spotted Wearing Anti-Trump Shirt at Left-Wing Event
sources.text:
Opinion | The author's opinion does not necessarily reflect Sarah Palin's view.
Former special counsel Jack Smith was photographed at a politically charged music festival in Maryland wearing a Bruce Springsteen shirt emblazoned with the phrase “No Kings.” Critics have long-speculated that Smith’s prosecutions of Donald Trump were politically biased because former AG Merrick Garland appointed him special counsel three days after Trump announced his 2024 campaign.
The cases against Trump were pushed toward trial in an election year, and investigators sought phone records of Republican lawmakers. Trump has called the indictments a corrupt effort to damage his campaign. Despite Smith’s denial of partisan motive, critics say his decision to sport this t-shirt removes all doubt.
Smith attended the Power to the People Fest at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, Maryland. Photos and videos posted by attendees showed him moving through the crowd, talking with concertgoers and posing for pictures. In some of the footage, Smith could also be seen holding a beer while speaking with people nearby.
One person who attended the event told The Daily Beast that Smith was taking selfies with “fans” throughout the festival. The black shirt Smith wore was tied to Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band’s “Land of Hope and Dreams” tour.
It prominently featured the words “No Kings,” a phrase that has become associated with demonstrations opposing President Donald Trump and his use of executive authority. The festival itself featured several musicians who have been outspoken critics of Trump and Republican policies.
Performers included Springsteen, the Foo Fighters and Joan Baez. Organizers promoted the event as a way for Americans to use music, political participation and civic action to influence the direction of the country.
A portion of ticket proceeds was also designated for VoteRiders, an organization that assists people with voter-identification issues.
During his performance, Springsteen played “Streets of Minneapolis” and criticized U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement from the stage.
The festival’s political tone continued in the closing remarks.
Tom Morello told the audience he hoped they had been “energized, radicalized, revolutionized, democratized.”
Smith also received a public shoutout during the Foo Fighters’ set.
[aa_gallery id=”992670″]
Singer Dave Grohl dedicated “My Hero” to “my new friend Jack” while Smith was in attendance.
Grohl also referenced questioning Smith faced from Sen. Eric Schmitt during a Senate hearing earlier in the week.
The concert appearance came shortly after Smith returned to the public spotlight through that Senate Judiciary Committee hearing.
Smith has repeatedly maintained that his investigations involving Trump and Trump allies were driven by evidence and the law rather than partisan politics.
In his final report, Smith said neither he nor his prosecutors acted for political reasons and described the office’s “north star” as following the facts and the law.
He has also rejected accusations that politics influenced the prosecutions.
At an October 2025 appearance, Smith called such claims “ludicrous.”
During the September 29, 2026, Senate hearing, Smith again said he held no partisan loyalty and argued that he would have pursued the same charges against a Democrat under the same set of facts.
His appearance at a festival filled with anti-Trump themes and performers therefore drew added attention, particularly because of the “No Kings” shirt and the enthusiastic reception he received from some attendees.

sources.news_title: Trump official flips lid over viral Jack Smith clip
sources.text:
Congressional Republicans were recently fact-checked during a live hearing with former special counsel Jack Smith after they tried to claim he was in Atlanta conspiring with a separate prosecutor investigating President Donald Trump, even though their evidence actually proved he was in Maryland. But despite the GOP's humiliation, Trump's team is continuing its crusade against Smith.
Trump's communications director posted an angry X screed on Monday because he is upset at Smith for wearing an anti-Trump shirt at a rock concert.
"Steven Cheung tore into Jack Smith in an X post after the former special counsel, who previously investigated criminal allegations against the president, was photographed at an anti-Trump concert wearing a 'No Kings' protest T-shirt," reported The Daily Beast's Will Neal on Monday. In his post, Cheung complained that “Jack Smith is a scumbag who was the partisan attack rat for Democrats who weaponized the justice system against President Trump for political purposes. Don’t think they won’t go after innocent Americans again if they get their way.”
Neal reported, "Smith’s T-shirt was from the merch line for anti-Trump rocker Bruce Springsteen’s 'Land of Hope and Dreams' tour, during which Springsteen was often explicitly critical of the second Trump administration."
He continued, "The former special counsel, 57, wore the shirt while attending the 'Power to the People' festival in Maryland, organized by Rage Against the Machine and Audioslave guitarist Tom Morello, also a fervent Trump critic."
Despite Republican attempts to deflect from their hearing faux pas, the main story regarding the Smith testimony is the fact that Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-MO) accused Smith of perjuring himself when the attorney said he had not been to Atlanta in February 2024. Schmitt made this claim based on the fact that Smith had attended a basketball game with a team known as the "Hawks," but it turned out he was mixing up the University of Iowa Hawkeyes (who had played in Maryland) with the Atlanta Hawks. It later came out that Schmitt was warned the information, which he received from Trump's Justice Department, had not been vetted, but he went ahead with the line of questioning anyway.
“It would be funny if it weren’t so concerning,” journalist Jonathan Rauch told political analyst Charlie Sykes last week. “It just reminds us that the charges that are being used are totally bogus.” He cited as another example David Hearn, an Olympian wrongly charged with a felony charges when Trump blamed him for his own botching of the Reflecting Pool renovations.. “They fell apart at the touch of reality. They fell apart so badly that a federal judge dismissed the charges with prejudice. That almost never happens. But that means that the judge trusts the Justice Department so little that they’re not even allowed to bring back the charge no matter what they come up with. The judge is saying, we just can’t trust these people. So all these demonstrations of comic incompetence. They have a serious grim side, but it’s kind of a saving grace that the folks running MAGA are not more capable than they are.”

Donald Trump attacks Jack Smith over his Bruce Springsteen “No Kings” shirt

Trump addressed Smith’s appearance in a Truth Social post on Sunday. He shared a report about Smith’s festival appearance alongside his criticism. “Deranged Jack Smith is a Crooked Prosecutor!” Trump wrote.
The shirt came from Springsteen’s Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour merchandise. The “No Kings” phrase has become associated with protests criticizing Trump. The dispute between Donald Trump and Jack Smith drew attention because of Smith’s previous investigations involving Trump.
Smith served as special counsel during federal investigations involving Trump. Those investigations examined efforts surrounding the 2020 election and classified documents. The cases were later dropped after Trump returned to office.
Smith’s festival appearance followed a recent Senate Judiciary Committee hearing. Republican lawmakers questioned him about his investigations and their handling. Smith maintained that his prosecutorial decisions were based on evidence rather than politics.
The festival also produced notable moments involving Smith. Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl dedicated “My Hero” to “my new friend Jack.” Grohl also wore an Iowa Hawkeyes shirt during his performance.
That reference followed a Senate dispute involving Senator Eric Schmitt and Smith. Schmitt had questioned Smith about attending an Atlanta Hawks game in 2024. Schmitt said, “I think you’ve already perjured yourself,” during questioning.
Springsteen headlined the Maryland festival alongside artists including Joan Baez and Dave Matthews. The event was organized by Tom Morella and emphasized music, activism, and civic engagement. Springsteen also performed “Streets of Minneapolis” during the event.
Jack Smith’s “No Kings” shirt quickly became the focus of attention surrounding his appearance. Trump’s response added another political dimension to the festival sighting. Smith has not publicly responded to Trump’s latest criticism in the supplied reporting.

sources.news_title: Jack Smith Spotted at Maryland ‘No Kings’ Concert as New Records Detail Phone Tracking in Trump Probe
sources.text:
Former Special Counsel Jack Smith was seen over the weekend at a “No Kings” concert in Maryland, an event organized by a nonprofit critical of President Trump. Photos circulating online show Smith wearing a T-shirt associated with the anti-Trump movement.
The appearance came just days after Smith testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee, telling lawmakers that politics played no role in his investigation of Trump.
Separately, newly declassified FBI records released Monday by the White House Government Transparency Task Force have added new detail to questions about the scope of that investigation. The records show that Smith’s team tracked the phone activity of Susie Wiles, who was a top Trump adviser during the period in question and now serves as White House chief of staff, including her contacts with at least 21 attorneys affiliated with Trump.
One memo, dated March 24, 2023, describes a call between Wiles and an attorney connected to Trump that lasted 41 seconds. The memo also documents two earlier calls between Wiles and the same attorney, listing their exact times and durations.
After Wiles was interviewed by the FBI on April 7, investigators reviewed her phone records again, this time to identify what the records describe as “contacts of interest on the date of her FBI interview.” That review would have included calls made to and from Wiles both before and after her interview.
The investigation originally centered on whether Trump unlawfully retained classified documents after leaving office in 2021. Records reported earlier indicate the probe’s reach extended to communications involving members of Congress, journalists, and numerous phones connected to the Trump White House.
Smith’s investigation did not result in a conviction of Trump. The newly released records are being reviewed as part of continuing scrutiny of how the special counsel’s office conducted its inquiry.

sources.news_title: Jack Smith Sparks Donald Trump Outrage by Wearing 'No Kings' Shirt at Bruce Springsteen Show: 'Deranged Crooked Prosecutor'
sources.text:
Jack Smith Sparks Donald Trump Outrage by Wearing 'No Kings' Shirt at Bruce Springsteen Show: 'Deranged Crooked Prosecutor'
Oct. 5 2026, Published 11:19 a.m. ET
Jack Smith's latest stint has sparked Donald Trump outrage.
Recently, the former Justice Department special counsel was spotted wearing a "No Kings" shirt at a Bruce Springsteen show at a Maryland music festival.
This prompted President Trump to personally address him as he wrote on Truth Social, per News Break, "Deranged Jack Smith is a Crooked Prosecutor!"
Trump linked the post to a story from Just the News, which was headlined, "Ex-Special Counsel Jack Smith sports Springsteen 'No Kings' shirt at 'Power to the People Fest.'"
For those unversed, "No Kings" is the slogan of the nationwide protests against Trump.
In the pictures, Smith was seen holding a beer and wearing a black Springsteen "Land of Hope and Dreams" tour shirt.
Notably, Smith's public appearance came just days after a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing.
In the hearing, he firmly defended the two prosecutions he brought against Trump over the Republican’s efforts to undo the presidential election and his retention of classified records at his Mar-a-Lago estate.
Want OK! each day? Sign up here!
What Was the 'Power to the People' Fest About?
The 'Power to the People' star-studded protest festival at Columbia, Maryland’s Merriweather Post Pavilion, aimed to celebrate “peace, justice, solidarity, music and community action,” according to its mission statement, and promote voter turnout.
Organized by Rage Against the Machine’s Tom Morello, part of the ticket sales will benefit VoteRiders and HeadCount.
Additionally, many of the acts at the event were used to denounce recent actions conducted by the U.S. government.
Springsteen opened with “Streets of Minneapolis,” in response to the killings of Renée Good and Alex Pretti by federal immigration agents, per WJTV.
“The power and solidarity of the people of Minneapolis, of Minnesota, is an inspiration to the entire country,” Springsteen told the sold-out crowd. “Their strength and their commitment told us that this is still America, and this will not stand. They gave us hope. They showed us courage.”
What's more is that this event took place just a month before the midterm elections.
“I think the timing is a reminder that showing up matters. I’m not here to tell anyone what to think or how to vote,” Taylor Momsen, one of the performers, told The Associated Press, via ABC News.
“I hope people leave feeling connected, inspired to care about the people around them, and reminded that we all have a part to play in our communities. If the festival can create that feeling, I think that’s a win,” she added.

White House rips ‘scumbag’ ex-special counsel Jack Smith after he wears ‘No Kings’ shirt to Bruce Springsteen show
See more of our coverage in your search results.
WASHINGTON — The White House ripped former special counsel Jack Smith as a “partisan attack rat” Monday after he was photographed and videoed wearing a “No Kings” T-shirt at a Maryland concert over the weekend.
“Jack Smith is a scumbag who was the partisan attack rat for Democrats who weaponized the justice system against President Trump for political purposes,” White House communications director Steven Cheung said on X in response to the images of Smith, who brought two criminal cases against the commander in chief ahead of the 2024 election.
“Don’t think they won’t go after innocent Americans again if they get their way,” added Cheung.
Images showed Smith, 57, scooting to his seat at the Merriweather Post Pavilion concert venue in Columbia, Md. while nursing a beer and wearing a Bruce Springsteen and the E-Street Band shirt.
Smith testified last week before the Senate Judiciary Committee about the “Arctic Frost” FBI probe that led to his indictment of Trump for trying to reverse the 2020 election results and hoarding national security papers at Mar-a-Lago.
“I am not a politician and I have no partisan loyalty,” the longtime prosecutor said in his opening remarks to the panel. “My career has been dedicated to serving our country by upholding the rule of law and the core principles upon which our country was founded.”
Saturday’s “Power to the People” show featured Springsteen, the Foo Fighters, Public Enemy, Dave Matthews, and Joan Baez among other artists.
In May, Springsteen tore into Trump during a lengthy concert at Nationals Park in the nation’s capital, calling the president “racist,” “incompetent” and “treasonous.”
Smith’s DC-based indictment of Trump was withdrawn following the Republican’s victory in the 2024 presidential election over then-Vice President Kamala Harris.
The classified document case had earlier been thrown out by a South Florida federal judge who ruled that Smith had been unlawfully appointed by then-Attorney General Merrick Garland in November 2022, shortly after Trump announced his third consecutive run for president.
Republicans in Congress who investigated Smith’s approach in both cases accused the former prosecutor of abusing his power, as when his team surreptitiously gained access to lawmakers’ text messages and call logs as part of the “Arctic Frost” probe.
Trump’s White House Government Transparency Task Force released declassified memos and emails Monday that showed the FBI was monitoring future White House chief of staff Susie Wiles’ phone calls.
The trap-and-trace method was just one of several ways the bureau was keeping tabs on the future president’s activities in the lead-up to the classified documents indictment through a probe known as “Plasmic Echo.”

sources.news_title: Jack Smith leaves Senate grilling behind — turns up at anti-Trump festival in a ‘No Kings’ shirt
sources.text:
BS BULLETIN:
- Former special counsel Jack Smith surfaced Saturday at the politically charged Power to the People Festival in Maryland.
- Smith wore a Bruce Springsteen “No Kings” shirt just days after defending his Trump investigations before the Senate Judiciary Committee.
- Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl appeared to salute Smith from the stage, dedicating “My Hero” to his “new friend Jack.”
Former special counsel Jack Smith apparently had plans for the weekend after his bruising appearance on Capitol Hill: a concert, a “No Kings” shirt and a crowd filled with some of President Donald Trump’s most outspoken cultural critics.
Smith was photographed Saturday at the Power to the People Festival at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, Maryland, wearing a black Bruce Springsteen shirt emblazoned with the anti-Trump slogan “No Kings.”
The appearance came only four days after Smith testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee about his investigations and prosecutions of Trump.
The festival was organized by Rage Against the Machine guitarist Tom Morello and featured Springsteen, Foo Fighters, Dave Matthews, Joan Baez, Killer Mike and others.
Smith attracted some attention of his own.
Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl appeared to give the former prosecutor a shout-out before the band launched into “My Hero.”
“This one goes out to my new friend Jack!” Grohl told the crowd.
Photos circulating from the festival showed concertgoers posing with Smith.
Springsteen, meanwhile, used his appearance to continue his criticism of the Trump administration, including an attack on federal immigration enforcement before performing his protest song “Streets of Minneapolis.”
The festival itself made no secret of its political component. Organizers described the event as bringing artists, activists and community leaders together to promote collective action, including around Election Day. A portion of ticket proceeds was designated for VoteRiders, a voting-access organization.
That makes Smith’s wardrobe notable because his political impartiality was one of the central issues raised by Republican senators only days earlier.
At Tuesday’s hearing, Smith defended his investigations as evidence-driven and rejected Republican accusations that he had weaponized federal law enforcement against Trump and his political allies.
Sen. Ted Cruz accused Smith of succeeding “where Richard Nixon failed,” alleging that his investigations represented the weaponization of the Justice Department against political opponents.
Sen. John Kennedy also pressed Smith over investigators obtaining non-content phone records involving Republican lawmakers. Smith maintained that the records sought were relevant to the investigation and that his team followed the law.
Smith’s Saturday outing does not establish that his prosecutions were politically motivated. But appearing at an explicitly political festival in anti-Trump merchandise only days after publicly defending the neutrality of those investigations is certain to provide fresh ammunition to critics who have questioned his impartiality.
MY QUICK TAKE
This is one of those stories where the timing does most of the work.
Jack Smith spent Tuesday insisting that evidence — not politics — drove his prosecution of Donald Trump. By Saturday he’s photographed at a politically charged festival wearing “No Kings” across his chest while one of the bands apparently dedicates “My Hero” to him.
None of that retroactively proves anything about a federal prosecution. Personal political expression after leaving government is not evidence of prosecutorial misconduct.
But Washington has always understood the importance of appearances. Justice Department rules and traditions surrounding political activity exist precisely because prosecutors wield extraordinary power and public confidence in their neutrality matters.
Smith is no longer special counsel, so he can wear whatever shirt he wants. But after years of Republicans arguing that his Trump investigations were political, perhaps the “World’s Most Impartial Former Prosecutor” coffee mug would have been the subtler choice.

sources.text:
Jack Smith attends anti-Trump concert wearing 'No Kings' shirt after Senate hearing
WASHINGTON (TNND) — Former special counsel Jack Smith attended an anti-President Trump concert wearing a "No Kings" shirt after he testified in a Senate hearing about his probes into the president last week.
Smith was at the Power to the People Festival in Columbia, Md., on Saturday, which Rage Against the Machine guitarist and socialist demonstrator Tom Morello organized, and featured Trump critic Bruce Springsteen, who gave a speech against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement before singing, Mediaite reported.
Foo Fighters lead singer Dave Grohl gave a shoutout while breaking into “My Hero.”
“This one goes out to my new friend Jack!” Grohl said.
Photos posted on X showed Smith wearing a black Springsteen shirt that reads, “No Kings.”
While on stage, Springsteen said ICE brought “death and terror to the streets of Minneapolis.” He released a song earlier this year condemning Trump and his “federal thugs” for their crackdown on illegal immigration, after the shooting death of Alex Pretti.
According to the festival’s website, the goal of the event was to bring together “artists, fans, activists, organizations and community leaders for an unforgettable day celebrating the power of music and collective action to inspire change.” The website said a “portion of the proceeds from all ticket sales plus 100% of the net proceeds from VIP tickets will be donated to VoteRiders,” a left-leaning organization.
The event followed Smith's testimony before the Senate on Tuesday about his former probes into Trump.
Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, accused Smith of leading “disgraceful” investigations that would go down in history as the “most egregious abuse of power in the history of the Department of Justice.” Cruz claimed Smith’s “witch hunt” against Trump and other Republicans were the result of him wanting to bring down his political enemies.
“Let me say congratulations, because you have succeeded where Richard Nixon failed, which is weaponizing the Department of Justice to go after your political opponents,” Cruz said. “Congratulations.”
Smith brought two indictments against Trump during his time out of office — one related to the alleged mishandling of classified documents, and another tied to Trump's alleged efforts to overturn the results of the 2020 election. The former special counsel defended the integrity of both investigations during the hearing.
"Our investigation developed proof beyond a reasonable doubt that President Trump engaged in serious crimes against our nation," Smith said. "If asked whether to prosecute a former president today based on the same facts, I would do so regardless of whether that president was a Republican or a Democrat."

sources.news_title: Jack Smith wears “No Kings” shirt at protest festival
sources.text:
Former special counsel Jack Smith was spotted at a music festival on October 3 wearing a "No Kings" T-shirt.
Smith, the attorney who led two criminal cases against then-former President Donald Trump in 2023, found himself at the center of an unexpectedly viral moment last week when Senator Eric Schmitt’s "slam dunk" evidence against him during a Senate Judiciary Committee quickly crumbled.
This weekend, Smith attended the inaugural Power to the People festival in Maryland, where his outfit quickly gained attention. Smith was wearing a T-shirt from Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band's Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour earlier this year.
The black top featured the text "Land of Hope & Dreams American Tour," "Springsteen & E Street," and, at the bottom, the words "No Kings."
What Is ‘No Kings’?
The term "No Kings" comes from a group of nonpartisan protests held across the U.S. opposing Donald Trump’s second administration.
Three nationwide No Kings protests have taken place so far, in June and October 2025 and in March 2026. The group also hosted a concert to rival Trump’s concert at the UFC Freedom 250 fight on June 14, 2026.
"The president thinks his rule is absolute. But in America, we don’t have kings—and we won’t back down against chaos, corruption, and cruelty," the No Kings website reads.
Smith wearing a T-shirt featuring the "No Kings" slogan is particularly notable given his role in the investigations into Trump. Smith was tasked with investigating Trump's efforts to overturn the 2020 election and the January 6, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol.
In a post on Truth Social on Sunday morning, Trump reacted to Smith being pictured in the T-shirt and wrote: "Deranged Jack Smith is a Crooked Prosecutor!"

Beyond the "No Kings" T-shirt, former special counsel Smith got an onstage shout out from the Foo Fighters.
Lead singer Dave Grohl dedicated the band’s 1997 hit "My Hero" to "my new friend Jack" as Smith watched on from the crowd.

The team's name was at the center of an embarrassing mix-up for Schmitt during his questioning of Smith last week in the Senate.
Believing he had found the smoking gun to support his theory that Smith and Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis had colluded on their investigations into Trump's election interference, Schmitt gloated about evidence that Smith was at an Atlanta Hawks game in February 2024.
However, the senator had confused the Atlanta Hawks with the Hawkeyes, and, in reality, Smith was not at the Hawks game, but watching the Iowa Hawkeyes team play nearly 600 miles away in Maryland.
What Happened at the Power to the People Festival?
Saturday’s Power to the People festival, hosted in Columbia, Maryland, was organized by Rage Against the Machine and Audioslave musician Tom Morello.
Described as a day of "peace, love, justice, and music," the lineup included Bruce Springsteen, Foo Fighters, Public Enemy and other artists.
On the website, the festival pledged that a portion of the proceeds from all ticket sales, and 100 percent of net proceeds from VIP tickets, would be donated to VoteRiders, a charity organization that helps citizens secure voter ID and promotes every U.S. citizen’s right to vote.
On stage, artists used the platform to speak out on issues close to them.
During their performance, Public Enemy front man Chuck D took aim at Ed Sheeran in the wake of rapper Macklemore being removed from his U.S. tour over pro-Palestinian remarks.
"This concert is not by Ed Sheeran’s promoters. Free Palestine, free Haiti, and please free a closed mind," Chuck D said, before adding: "F*** Donald Trump."
In another onstage speech, event organizer Morello told the audience: "This land does not belong to the billionaires and the oligarchs. It does not belong to the racists and the warmongers. It does not belong to the fascists and the would-be dictators. Brothers and sisters, this land belongs to you and me. Power to the people!"

sources.news_title: Jack Smith Appears at Anti-Trump Maryland Festival in ‘No Kings’ Shirt as Foo Fighters Dedicate ‘My Hero’ to Him
sources.text:
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom.
Former Special Counsel Jack Smith made a conspicuous appearance Saturday at a Maryland music festival featuring extensive criticism of President Donald Trump, wearing a “No Kings” shirt before receiving an onstage dedication from Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl.
Smith attended the “Power to the People” festival at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, Maryland, where Bruce Springsteen, Foo Fighters, Tom Morello, Joan Baez and other performers appeared at an event combining live music with political activism. The festival was organized by Morello and promoted participation by activist organizations ahead of the November midterm elections.
Photographs from the event showed Smith wearing a black shirt reading, “Bruce Springsteen & E Street Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour No Kings.” Smith served as special counsel during the Biden administration and led two federal criminal investigations of Trump before leaving the Justice Department.
His appearance quickly drew attention because of both the overtly political nature of the festival and Smith’s previous insistence that his work as special counsel was conducted without partisan motivation.
Grohl acknowledged Smith from the stage before Foo Fighters performed one of the band’s best-known songs.
“This one goes out to my new friend Jack,” Grohl said before the band began “My Hero.” Contemporary reports and footage from the festival identified Smith as the person Grohl was addressing.
The festival itself featured repeated criticism of the Trump administration. Springsteen, one of Trump’s longtime celebrity critics, used his performance to condemn administration policies and immigration enforcement, while other performers and speakers incorporated political messages into their appearances. Activists at the event were also heard chanting “Free Palestine.”
The Associated Press described the gathering as an activist-oriented event centered on “peace, justice, community and voter turnout,” with a “Freedom Village” where political and advocacy organizations interacted with concertgoers. Springsteen headlined the festival, while Morello, Baez, Grohl and other musicians participated throughout the day.
Smith’s attendance came only days after a contentious Sept. 29 appearance before the Senate Judiciary Committee, where Republicans accused him of exceeding his authority and conducting politically motivated investigations of Trump and Republican figures. Smith rejected those allegations and said his prosecutorial decisions were based on evidence and Justice Department rules rather than politics.
Republican lawmakers have focused particularly on the breadth of an investigation known as Arctic Frost, which preceded and became part of Smith’s federal investigation into efforts surrounding the 2020 presidential election.
Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, disclosed records that he said showed investigators obtained at least 4,782 checks written by people who had made mostly small-dollar donations to Trump or Trump-aligned Republican organizations between September 2019 and August 2023. The checks contained information including donors’ names, addresses, bank routing and account numbers and signatures, according to the committee.
Smith acknowledged during the hearing that his office obtained financial information while conducting the criminal investigation but defended the use of subpoenas as part of legitimate investigative activity.
Grassley and other Republicans have argued that the scope of the records collection went far beyond what was necessary to investigate Trump and violated the privacy of Americans whose political donations brought their banking information into the investigation. Smith disputed the broader characterization that his operation targeted people because they were Republicans.
The Republican-led committee has also scrutinized Smith’s pursuit of telephone records associated with lawmakers and other information obtained during the investigation. Committee records released in 2026 showed that telecommunications companies received dozens of subpoenas, including requests involving current and former Republican members of Congress.
Democrats on the Judiciary Committee have defended Smith and argued that investigators were following evidence related to Trump’s efforts to challenge the outcome of the 2020 presidential election. Ranking Democrat Dick Durbin of Illinois said during the hearing that Smith’s investigation was legitimate and rejected Republican allegations that it represented politically motivated misconduct.
The hearing also produced disputes over Smith’s previous descriptions of what investigators obtained from lawmakers’ communications. Republican critics have accused him of providing inconsistent testimony about whether investigators received only telephone metadata or, in some instances, the contents of communications.
Claims circulating after the hearing that Smith committed perjury have not resulted in a criminal charge or judicial finding that he lied under oath. Smith and his defenders have distinguished between telephone toll records — information showing details such as who contacted whom and when — and other communications obtained through separate investigative processes. The Senate committee’s Democratic staff emphasized during questioning that Smith described toll records as metadata rather than the contents of calls or messages.
Republicans, however, have continued investigating broader records showing that communications involving members of Congress, journalists and other individuals were obtained during the federal investigation. Grassley’s office has said records disclosed to the committee show investigators collected communications involving journalists at numerous national media organizations as well as information connected to lawmakers.
Smith was appointed special counsel in November 2022 by then-Attorney General Merrick Garland. He ultimately brought two separate federal criminal cases against Trump.
One charged Trump over alleged efforts to overturn the results of the 2020 election and events leading to the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot. The other accused Trump of illegally retaining classified national-security records after leaving the White House and obstructing efforts to recover them.
Trump pleaded not guilty and repeatedly characterized both prosecutions as politically motivated efforts to damage his campaign to return to the White House.
The 2020 election case was dismissed at Smith’s request after Trump defeated Vice President Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. Smith cited the Justice Department’s longstanding position that a sitting president cannot be criminally prosecuted, making Trump’s return to office decisive in ending the federal case. The dismissal was not based on a determination that the charges lacked merit.
The classified-documents case had previously been dismissed by U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon, who ruled in July 2024 that Smith’s appointment violated the Constitution. Smith appealed that ruling, but following Trump’s election victory, the Justice Department abandoned its effort to continue prosecuting Trump as he prepared to return to office.
Throughout his tenure, Smith rejected Trump’s assertions that the investigations were politically directed. He repeated that position before the Senate Judiciary Committee, saying he would have pursued the same evidence regardless of the political party or position of the person involved.
Republican senators have remained unconvinced, pointing to the timing, reach and investigative tactics employed by Smith’s team. Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, sharply criticized Smith during last week’s hearing, accusing him of weaponizing federal law enforcement against a political opponent. Smith rejected Cruz’s characterization.
Against that backdrop, Smith’s decision to attend Saturday’s anti-Trump-oriented festival wearing a “No Kings” shirt immediately attracted new criticism from conservatives who argue the appearance raises questions about the political views of the former prosecutor who pursued Trump.
Smith is no longer a Justice Department employee and, as a private citizen, is free to attend political events and express political views. His appearance Saturday does not by itself establish that his previous prosecutorial decisions were politically motivated.
The optics nevertheless drew attention because Smith spent years at the center of one of the country’s most politically consequential federal prosecutions and appeared at the Maryland festival only days after defending the independence of those investigations before Congress.
The crowd Saturday saw a markedly different side of the former special counsel: rather than sitting before senators defending subpoenas and prosecutorial decisions, Smith stood among concertgoers in a “No Kings” shirt as Grohl dedicated “My Hero” to his “new friend Jack.”

Fox News detailed the activist network surrounding the festival, including partner organizations mobilizing voters ahead of Election Day and a VIP program whose proceeds were directed to nonprofits focused on human rights and social justice; the report also noted that Ben & Jerry’s and several advocacy groups were promoted as community partners. sources.news_title: Jack Smith enrages Trump by wearing 'No Kings' shirt to Springsteen show
sources.text:
President Donald Trump went after former special counsel Jack Smith on Sunday, a day after photos of Smith at a Maryland music festival spread across social media.
"Deranged Jack Smith is a Crooked Prosecutor!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.
His post linked to a Just the News story headlined "Ex-Special Counsel Jack Smith sports Springsteen 'No Kings' shirt at 'Power to the People Fest.'"
Smith went to the festival on Saturday. It was organized by Rage Against the Machine guitarist Tom Morello, and Bruce Springsteen was on the lineup. Photos showed Smith holding a beer and wearing a black Springsteen "Land of Hope and Dreams" tour shirt that read "No Kings," the slogan of the nationwide protests against Trump.
Fans said people were high-fiving Smith and lining up for selfies.
Foo Fighters frontman Dave Grohl also seemed to acknowledge him from the stage. Grohl wore an Iowa Hawkeyes T-shirt during his set, which the music site Consequence called a "not-so-subtle reference" to Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.). He then dedicated "My Hero" to "my new friend Jack."
The shirt was a jab at Schmitt's failed attempt at a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on Tuesday to accuse Smith of perjury. Schmitt claimed Smith lied about attending an Atlanta Hawks game in February 2024 and held up text messages he said proved it. "I think you've already perjured yourself," Schmitt said.
It later came out that Smith had actually been watching Caitlin Clark and the Iowa Hawkeyes.
Smith led multiple federal investigations into Trump, including one over his efforts to overturn the 2020 election and one over his handling of classified documents. Those two cases were dropped after Trump won the 2024 election.

sources.news_title: Jack Smith Turns Up at Star-Studded Anti-Trump Festival — President Trump Notices
sources.text:
Jack Smith spent years telling the country that his pursuit of Donald Trump was about the law, not politics.
Then the former special counsel turned up at a star-studded anti-Trump music festival in Maryland wearing a Bruce Springsteen “No Kings” shirt.
That is a choice. And President Trump noticed.
Video circulating from Saturday night showed Smith in the crowd at the inaugural “Power to the People” festival at Merriweather Post Pavilion:
The event was billed as a celebration of music, civic action and voter participation. Its lineup included Springsteen, Foo Fighters, John Legend, Dave Matthews, the Chicks and Public Enemy, with Rage Against the Machine guitarist Tom Morello serving as organizer.
But there was nothing politically mysterious about the evening.
The Associated Press reported that Springsteen headlined the inaugural event at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, Maryland, after Morello organized a bill that also included Foo Fighters, John Legend, Dave Matthews, the Chicks, Public Enemy and other prominent performers; organizers described the mission as peace, justice, solidarity, music and community action, while a portion of ticket proceeds went to VoteRiders and HeadCount. The politics were just as clear from the stage and across the packed amphitheater that Saturday night, with the event arriving one month before Election Day and deliberately connecting celebrity performances to political organizing: Springsteen opened with “Streets of Minneapolis,” a protest song targeting federal immigration enforcement, Grandson performed “My President’s a Felon,” and the crowd was repeatedly urged to turn its energy into votes before the midterm elections.
The crowd did not have to decode the message. The night was designed to move people from applause to political action.
Fox News detailed the activist network surrounding the festival, including partner organizations mobilizing voters ahead of Election Day and a VIP program whose proceeds were directed to nonprofits focused on human rights and social justice; the report also noted that Ben & Jerry’s and several advocacy groups were promoted as community partners. Morello made the event’s posture explicit from the stage by attacking “dictators” and “oligarchs,” while Springsteen continued the anti-Trump message that has defined his recent political appearances, leaving little daylight between the night’s entertainment and its election-year purpose.
Smith did not blend into the audience. He wore a “No Kings” shirt from Springsteen’s merchandise line—a slogan that has become a rallying cry of the anti-Trump protest movement.
The choice quickly became the story:
Ex-Special Counsel Jack Smith wears Springsteen ‘No Kings’ shirt at ‘Power to the People Fest’ in Maryland https://t.co/wPfydbNkHE
— Off The Press (@OffThePress1) October 4, 2026
Smith is a private citizen. He has every right to attend a concert, buy a shirt and make his politics visible.
But the optics are impossible to dismiss.
Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed Smith in November 2022 to oversee two investigations of Trump. At the time, the Justice Department said the appointment would protect the work’s independence and described Smith as the person to handle the cases in an “even-handed” manner.
Smith went on to bring two federal criminal cases against Trump—one concerning classified documents and another concerning the 2020 election. Those cases consumed years of national attention and helped define the 2024 campaign.
They were ultimately abandoned after Trump won the election and returned to the White House.
Throughout it all, Americans were repeatedly told to trust the institutional separation between prosecution and politics, even as the cases reached directly into a presidential election.
That trust was already badly damaged. A former special counsel publicly adopting the visual language of the movement opposing the man he prosecuted does not repair it.
Trump responded Sunday morning by sharing coverage of Smith’s appearance and reviving his familiar charge that Smith was a politically motivated prosecutor:
Deranged Jack Smith is a Crooked Prosecutor! President DJT
Ex-Special Counsel Jack Smith sports Springsteen ‘No Kings’ shirt at ‘Power to the People Fest’:https://t.co/k9QwAE8QG2
( TS: Oct 4 2026, 10:10 AM ET ) pic.twitter.com/fT7lIL2Vja
— Commentary Donald J. Trump Truth Social Posts On X (@TrumpTruthOnX) October 4, 2026
None of this proves that Smith made a dishonest decision inside the special counsel’s office. That claim would require evidence far beyond a concert appearance.
What it does prove is that the public’s skepticism was never irrational.
Prosecutors entrusted with extraordinary power must avoid bias and guard the appearance of impartiality—especially when the target is a presidential candidate and the cases can alter the course of an election.
Smith knew the stakes. He also knew exactly what “No Kings” meant in that room.
He made his statement anyway.

sources.text:
Ex-Special Counsel Jack Smith sports Springsteen ‘No Kings’ shirt at ‘Power to the People Fest’
The event was held in Maryland to demonstrate the “power everyday human beings have when they come together — through music, art, community and action — to shape our country and our planet on, and beyond, Election Day.”
Former Special Counsel Jack Smith was spotted sporting a Bruce Springsteen "No Kings" shirt at the "Power to the People Fest" on Saturday in Maryland.

He performed his anti-ICE protest song, "Streets of Minneapolis."

The shirt is from his recent "Land of Hope and Dreams" American tour.
This marked the first public sighting of Smith since his Senate hearing on Tuesday. 
image credit: @MissusLakey on X
"Foo Fighters" lead singer Dave Grohl reportedly dedicated a song from his set to his favorite Jack, which was apparently a reference to Smith. 
The event was held in Maryland near Washington, DC to demonstrate the “power everyday human beings have when they come together — through music, art, community and action — to shape our country and our planet on, and beyond, Election Day.”
Guitarist Tom Morello from "Rage Against the Machine" organized the festival. 
“Hopefully you’ve been energized, radicalized, revolutionized, democratized and wound the f–k up," Morello said when closing out the festival.
